wants.evidence: Shri Leela Charitam's top videos (e.g., 'Bholenath being scolded by an old woman') show that viewers love seeing God in domestic, mundane, or humorous human situations.
Kalia Katha and Bhakti Magic consistently perform well when the narrative focuses on a specific moral lesson or a unique interaction between a devotee and Krishna.
Gyan Adhyatmik Katha's extreme spikes during Dhanteras prove that timely, ritual-focused content for upcoming festivals is in massive demand.
Krishn Kehte Hai's high performance on 'Who was Gayasur?' or 'Mahishasur' suggests viewers want deep-dives into the origins and backstories of mythological figures.

gaps: High-quality 3D animation for lesser-known Puranic characters
Detailed explanations of why specific rituals are performed (beyond just the story)
Content bridging the gap between ancient scripture and modern-day life problems
saturated: General summaries of the Ramayana or Mahabharata without a unique angle
Generic 'Ekadashi Vrat' stories that lack a hook or visual differentiation
Over-dramatized thumbnails that don't match the video content (viewers are starting to complain about clickbait)
title_patterns: Use of '😱' emoji in titles to signal a shocking or miraculous event
